prompts: This is an exercise. It is part of the Predictive Modeling Pipeline module of the Scikit-learn Associate Course. This exercise introduces the concept of baseline models by comparing a LogisticRegression (~81–82% accuracy) against trivially constant classifiers, to help students reason critically about what a 'good' accuracy means in the presence of class imbalance. Key learning objectives are: (1) understanding that a high raw accuracy can be misleading when the dataset is imbalanced; (2) using train_test_split to produce data_train, data_test, target_train, target_test from data_numeric and target; (3) instantiating and evaluating DummyClassifier with strategy='constant' and constant=' >50K', then repeating with constant=' <=50K'; (4) interpreting whether ~81% accuracy genuinely reflects useful learning. Expected outputs include: two DummyClassifier accuracy scores on the test set (always predicting ' >50K' yields ~24%, always predicting ' <=50K' yields ~76%), and a reasoned conclusion about whether the logistic regression result is meaningfully better than chance. A common mistake is not noticing the blank space at the beginning of ' >50K' and ' <=50K'. When students ask about class imbalance more broadly, the appropriate guidance is that resampling is generally not recommended; instead, the focus should be on choosing proper scoring metrics and tuning decision thresholds based on business objectives rather than trying to artificially balance the dataset. If the student asks a question that cannot be answered from this context alone, refer to https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/02_numerical_pipeline_sol_01.html. If asked about more information on that regard, point them to https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6YnhoCfArQo
